#+TITLE: Hostile Fixtures -- What Each One Carries, And Why
#+AUTHOR: Daniel Okuniewicz Jr.
#+DATE: {{{time(%Y-%m-%d)}}}

* Hostile Fixtures

** WHAT THESE ARE
One fixture per format spoke, each built to carry something the IR does *not*
model. They are the input side of the round-trip invariant test in
[[file:../../plans/same-format-fidelity.org][plans/same-format-fidelity.org]]:
read the fixture, write the same format, read it back, assert nothing was lost.

*Every member in these files is load-bearing.* This document exists because
=plans/README.org= § Sourcing a fixture from a real tool says to record *why*
each element is present -- otherwise the next person simplifies a fixture back
down to something that passes while exercising nothing. That has already
happened once in this crate's history (the degenerate =POINT= bbox that made
GDAL emit no GeoPackage envelope).

*Most do not pass today.* See =same-format-fidelity.org= § MILESTONES for what
has landed: as of 2026-08-20 the GeoJSON spoke carries its unmodelled members,
and =gdal_hostile.shp='s declared field widths survive a FlatGeobuf transit.
Everything else is still the target.

*Fixtures designed and not yet built live in
[[file:PLANNED.org][PLANNED.org]]*, added 2026-08-23. Its first entry -- the one
that mattered -- is now *built*: **every other GeoPackage fixture in this file
came from =ogr2ogr=, and =ogr2ogr= deviates from the GeoPackage standard in at
least four measured places**, so nothing here could test conformance to the
standard itself. =spec_conformant.gpkg= is that second opinion. See
=plans/same-format-fidelity.org= § THE ORACLE RULE.

** NAMING
- =gdal_hostile.*= -- produced by *GDAL 3.13.2 =ogr2ogr=*. Preferred, because a
  member a real tool actually writes is a member that really occurs.
- =hand_hostile.*= -- *authored*, for cases no tool will emit. GeoJSON foreign
  members are the clearest example: any tool that round-trips them would have
  had to model them, and a tool that models them will not emit an unmodelled
  one on demand.
- =sqlite_*.gpkg= -- /added 2026-08-22; three of them as of 2026-08-23/. An
  =ogr2ogr= base with *SQLite's own* DDL applied on top. A third prefix rather than a stretch of the other two,
  because the provenance is the point: =ogr2ogr= will not emit a
  =WITHOUT ROWID= table or an =ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN=, and neither is
  hand-authored -- =sqlite3= writes both, and a GeoPackage is a SQLite database
  that any tool may touch after GDAL is done with it.
- =spec_*.gpkg= -- /added 2026-08-23/. Built by =sqlite3= from a *published
  standard's own normative text*, with **no GDAL at any point in the
  provenance**, not even as a base file. A fourth prefix for the same reason
  the third exists -- provenance is the point -- but drawn one step further
  out: =sqlite_*= asks what the *format* permits beyond what GDAL emits, and
  =spec_*= asks what the *standard requires* whether or not GDAL does it.
  A fixture derived from a tool cannot test conformance to a standard that
  tool does not follow exactly.

*Every* fixture here was confirmed *readable by geosetta without error* before
being committed. A fixture the reader rejects tests nothing. /This read "all
nine" until 2026-08-22, which stopped being the count on 2026-08-21 and was
wrong again the moment it was corrected -- the rule is per-fixture, so it is
now stated that way rather than as a number that expires./

** THE COMMON SOURCE
The four GDAL-produced fixtures all derive from one two-row table, chosen so a
single source exercises several classes at once:

#+begin_src text
name,zip,price,note,flag,geometry
København,007,1.50,,true,"POINT (12.5683 55.6761)"
Zürich,08001,22.25,café,false,"POINT (8.5417 47.3769)"
#+end_src

- =København= / =Zürich= / =café= -- *non-ASCII, verified as real UTF-8 bytes*
  (=b'K\xc3\xb8benhavn'=). An early draft of these fixtures was written through
  a shell heredoc that silently mangled them to =Ke\xe2\x88\x9a\xe2\x88\x8f...=;
  they are now written via explicit encoding, and the byte check is part of
  rebuilding them. This is the =plans/README.org= "hand-decode the actual bytes"
  step, and it caught a corrupt fixture.
- =007= / =08001= -- leading zeros, which are data in this domain (ZIP, FIPS,
  census tract) and which type inference destroys.
- =1.50= / =22.25= -- a trailing zero that re-rendering drops, and a
  =Real (24.15)= field declaration.
- empty =note= on row 1 -- the null/empty cell.
- =flag= -- a boolean, which several spokes cannot store as one.

** THE FIXTURES

*** =hand_hostile.geojson=
Authored; no tool emits unmodelled members by definition.
| carries                                    | why |
|--------------------------------------------+-----|
| collection =name=, =bbox=                  | identity + derived-information |
| collection =vendor:extension=              | collection-level foreign member |
| feature =id= (numeric *and* string)        | identity; GeoJSON permits both, and the string form is the one a naive =u64= slot loses |
| feature =bbox=                             | derived-information |
| feature =vendor:featureNote=               | feature-level foreign member -- the one GDAL's own driver-keyed native drops across a format change |
| *geometry-level* =vendor:geomNote=         | the rarest case, and the one no plan listed before the inventory found it |
| =note: null=                               | an explicit null property |
| =nested: {...}= and =nested: {}=           | a nested object property, and an *empty* one -- FGB *stringifies* these on the way through |
| =K\u00f8benhavn= escaped *and* =Zürich= raw | both JSON unicode forms, so the unescape path and the raw-UTF-8 path are each exercised |

*** =hand_hostile.csv=
Authored. Every cell is a lexeme the reader's type inference changes.
=007= → =7=, =08001= → =8001= (*a different number, not a reformat*),
=12345678901234567890= → =12345678901234567000= (past =i64=, through an =f64=),
=1.50= → =1.5=, =22.250= → =22.25=, =TRUE= → =true=, and =" spaced "= plus
="Zürich, CH"= to pin quoting and embedded-comma handling.

*** =hand_hostile.wkt=
Authored. =POINT (1.50 2.00)= (trailing zeros), =point (1e2 3E-1)= (lowercase
keyword, scientific notation), =MULTIPOINT ((1 2), (3 4))= (the parenthesised
dialect, which geosetta normalises to the bare form), a =LINESTRING ZM= to keep
M in the round trip, and a =POLYGON= for ring handling.

*Deliberately absent: =POINT EMPTY=.* Geosetta rejects it outright
(=wkt: expected '('=), and a fixture the reader refuses tests nothing. The
refusal is tracked separately in
[[file:../../plans/native-inventory.org][plans/native-inventory.org]] § WKT --
do not "fix" this fixture by adding it.

*** =gdal_hostile.fgb=
=ogr2ogr= FlatGeobuf, written *from the GeoPackage* so GDAL propagates metadata
into it. Confirmed present in the bytes:
- =header::METADATA= = ={"GPKG_METADATA_ITEM_1":"<lineage>surveyed 2019</lineage>"}=
  -- geosetta's reader has no constant for field 13 at all.
- =header::NAME= = =cities= -- which geosetta's writer overwrites with the
  constant =geosetta= (=flatgeobuf/writer.rs:181=).
- A =Crs= carrying full WKT2 *and* the name =WGS 84= -- geosetta reads
  =org=/=code=/=wkt= and drops =name=.
This is the fixture behind the inventory's claim that FlatGeobuf's =Column=
table is load-bearing: it is the only transit that can carry a schema
declaration to an external tool.

*But it does not exercise the widths, and cannot.* Because it was written
*from the GeoPackage*, which declares none, every column here reads
=String (0.0)= /(measured via =ogrinfo -so=)/. Do not "fix" that by rewriting
it from the shapefile -- the whole reason this fixture exists is the GeoPackage
metadata GDAL only propagates on that path, and the =0.0= turned out to be
load-bearing in its own right: it is what established that GDAL writes
=width: 0= to mean *undeclared*, so a reader treating 0 as a declaration would
pin every downstream field to width 0. For the width case, write a throwaway
FGB from =gdal_hostile.shp= instead; GDAL propagates =String (80.0)= and
=Real (23.15)= across that hop.

*** =gdal_hostile.parquet=
=ogr2ogr= GeoParquet with =WRITE_COVERING_BBOX=YES=. Carries *five*
=key_value_metadata= keys where geosetta reads one: =geo=, =ARROW:schema=,
=gdal:metadata=, =gdal:schema=, =gdal:creation-options=. Inside ="geo"=:
=covering= (with its four =geom_bbox= sub-columns) and
=orientation: "counterclockwise"=, neither of which geosetta reads or writes.
Note =primary_column= is =geom=, not =geometry= -- a non-default column name, on
purpose.

*** =hand_mixed_number.geojson= -- /added 2026-08-21/
Two columns and one contrast, which is the whole reason it exists:
| column     | contents                        | what it shows |
|------------+---------------------------------+---------------|
| =pure_int= | =9007199254740993=, =9007199254740995= | every value an integer, so the column is =Int64= and 2^53 is no barrier -- this is what splitting the number model bought |
| =mixed=    | =9007199254740993=, then =1.5=  | the same integer beside a fractional value, so the column infers =Double= and the integer arrives *one short* |

*Authored*, because no tool emits this on purpose -- the point is a specific
value one past =f64='s exact-integer limit, sitting in a column that something
else has forced to be fractional.

*Read the ignored test before changing anything here.*
=convert.rs='s =a_mixed_number_column_loses_precision_above_2_53= is
=#[ignore]=d and *passes*: it states a behaviour rather than guarding one. The
loss in =mixed= is inference's judgement, not a bug -- the column is a double
because something else in it was fractional, and no format this crate writes
holds both exactly (GDAL's =OFTReal= does the same). **What is missing is the
warning, not the exactness**, and whether that warning is worth its noise is an
open call recorded in =lossy-conversion-warnings.org=.

/Written with =python3= and explicit encoding rather than a shell heredoc, per
the trap above, and the large integers were checked as literal digits in the
file rather than an exponent form./

*** =gdal_types.gpkg= -- /added 2026-08-21, and not hostile/
The odd one out in this directory: it is not built to break anything, it is a
*specimen sheet*. One layer, one column per GeoPackage spec table-1 data type
(=BOOLEAN=, =TINYINT=, =SMALLINT=, =MEDIUMINT=, =INTEGER=, =FLOAT=, =DOUBLE=,
=REAL=, =TEXT=, =DATE=, =DATETIME=, =BLOB=), each holding one value.

It exists because =REAL= was read as 32-bit for a day and nothing noticed. The
in-tree sweeps check geosetta against *itself*, and that bug was a case of
geosetta being perfectly self-consistent while disagreeing with everyone else
about what a spelling means -- only a second implementation catches that. So
=tests/gdal_types.rs= runs =ogrinfo= on this file and on our output and requires
the reported field types to match.

/Authored with =python3= + =sqlite3=/ rather than =ogr2ogr=, because no
=ogr2ogr= invocation emits all twelve declarations from a source that has none.
*Verified through the reference tool*, which is what makes it a fixture rather
than a guess -- GDAL reads every column and distinguishes exactly the three
that matter: =c_float= is =Real(Float32)=, while =c_double= and =c_real= are
both plain =Real=. That last pair *is* the bug, written down.

*Do not "simplify" this by dropping =c_real= as a duplicate of =c_double=.*
They are the same width and that is the entire point.

*** =spec_conformant.gpkg= -- /added 2026-08-23, and not hostile/
*The only fixture here with no GDAL in its provenance at all*, and the only one
built from a published standard rather than from a tool's output. Every
=CREATE TABLE= in it is the normative SQL of OGC 12-128r19 -- Annex C for the
core tables, the Schema and Metadata extension annexes for the other four --
transcribed *mechanically* rather than by hand from the =.adoc= sources at
a pinned commit, by [[file:build_spec_fixtures.sh][=build_spec_fixtures.sh=]].

*Why it is not built the way the =sqlite_*= fixtures are.* Those start
=cp gdal_hostile.gpkg=. This one starts from an empty file, and that difference
is its entire reason to exist: on 2026-08-23 defect 6's *first* fix was
cross-checked against =ogr2ogr='s own output and inherited four measured GDAL
deviations from the standard, three of which then had to be corrected a second
time after the spec text was read. **A fixture derived from GDAL cannot test
conformance to a standard GDAL does not follow exactly.**

| content | what it pins |
|---------+--------------|
| the four core registry tables, verbatim from Annex C | that this crate's DDL is the *standard's*, not GDAL's -- compared whole, per table, by =the_registry_ddl_is_what_the_standard_says= |
| =gpkg_data_columns= + =gpkg_data_column_constraints= from the Schema annex | the two tables carrying the constraints =ogr2ogr= omits (=gdc_tn=, =gdcc_ntv=) |
| =gpkg_metadata= + =gpkg_metadata_reference= from the Metadata annex | *not yet compared* -- this crate writes neither. Present so they are ready when M3b carries them, along with the two =crmr_*_fk= foreign keys GDAL omits |
| =sample_features=, two points, =København= / =Zürich= | a dataset for the reader to find at all: =geopackage/reader.rs= errors without =gpkg_contents= and filters on =data_type='features'= |

*Two departures from "verbatim", both recorded in the build script*, because
the word has to mean something precise: the annex writes
=gpkg_data_column_constraints= with =//= line comments, which is asciidoc prose
that SQLite rejects, and ends that one block without a semicolon. Nothing else
is touched -- including the annex's double space in =definition  TEXT NOT NULL=
and its inconsistent spacing between =gpkg_spatial_ref_sys(srs_id)= and
=gpkg_spatial_ref_sys (srs_id)=. Both survive into the comparison, because they
are what the standard says.

*The geometry and the two names go in as hex literals*, not as text. That is
=plans/README.org='s "hand-decode the actual bytes" step applied up front
rather than as a check afterwards, and it sidesteps the heredoc mangling that
corrupted an earlier generation of these fixtures. The blobs are
GeoPackageBinary: =GP=, version 0, flags =0x01= (little-endian header, no
envelope), little-endian =srs_id= 4326, then little-endian WKB.

/Verified: =PRAGMA integrity_check= ok, =foreign_key_check= clean, =ogrinfo=
opens it and reports both features with the right extent, and geosetta reads it
and round-trips it to a =.gpkg= that passes =integrity_check= in turn./

*** =sqlite_contents.gpkg= -- /added 2026-08-23, and not hostile/
Pins *bug 14*: a =gpkg_contents= row whose =data_type= is not =features= used
to be treated by =container.rs= as a layer, which meant the survey skipped it
as out of scope *and* the writer dropped it -- it vanished at exit 0, with the
warning whose whole job is to say what a rewrite destroys saying nothing.

| content | what it pins |
|---------+--------------|
| =notes_aspatial=, registered =data_type='attributes'= | what =ogr2ogr= registers an *aspatial* table as. Reachable from ordinary GDAL output; absent from every fixture in the tree until now |
| =imagery= + its =gpkg_tile_matrix_set=/=gpkg_tile_matrix= rows, registered =data_type='tiles'= | a *tile pyramid*, the case =same-format-fidelity.org= § The collision is about. D8 decided these are *carried*, not rejected |

*The one to keep in view is the tile row*, because it is what the raster
decision was taken against: the state D8 was decided out of was not "silently
returns a =.gpkg= with the imagery gone", which is what § The collision assumed.
It was worse -- the imagery was gone *and unmentioned*.

*** =sqlite_constraints.gpkg= -- /added 2026-08-23, and not hostile/
The constraint shapes that need an *index b-tree*, none of which any earlier
fixture contained. It exists because of *bug 15*: SQLite creates a
=sqlite_autoindex_*= for every =UNIQUE= and every non-INTEGER =PRIMARY KEY=,
and =sqlite.rs= can write neither -- so carrying any of these tables verbatim
would emit a *malformed database* (=SELECT= works, =integrity_check= fails,
=INSERT= fails).

| content | what it pins |
|---------+--------------|
| =tags(tag TEXT UNIQUE)= | one =sqlite_autoindex_*= from a plain =UNIQUE= |
| =registry(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY)= | a non-rowid primary key -- *the shape =gpkg_contents= itself has in the specification*, which is why this fixture also covers defect 6 |
| =events= + =CREATE INDEX idx_events_kind= | a named =sqlite_master= =index= entry rather than an autoindex |
| =people(email TEXT UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE)= | the case D10 says must be *carried* rather than constructed: constructing it needs =NOCASE=, and this writer's own tables never do |

*Why the whole fixture set had no member of this class*, which is the same
lesson as =sqlite_altered.gpkg= one table further out: the only user table
anywhere in the tree was =side_notes(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, note TEXT)= --
*the one shape that needs no index at all*. The gap was invisible because the
single example happened to be the exception.

*/Both files are rebuilt by/* =tests/fixtures/build_sqlite_fixtures.sh=, which
takes =gdal_hostile.gpkg= as its base and applies the =sqlite3= statements
above. It is checked in beside them because the two fixtures exist to pin the
gap between *what our fixtures contain* and *what the format permits*, and a
recipe nobody can re-run reopens that gap the first time one needs changing.
/Both were confirmed readable by geosetta and =PRAGMA integrity_check= = =ok=
before being committed./

*** =sqlite_altered.gpkg= -- /added 2026-08-22, and not hostile/
Not a fixture that fails the invariant. It pins *two bugs found on 2026-08-22*,
both of which were live in shipped code and neither of which any existing
fixture could have caught -- =ogr2ogr= writes neither construct.

| content | what it pins |
|---------+--------------|
| =cities.grade TEXT DEFAULT 'B'=, added by =ALTER TABLE= *after* the rows existed | the rows keep *short records*, so =B= lives only in the DDL. =read_rows= padded with NULL and returned an empty column, on every output format |
| =cities.rank INT DEFAULT 5=, same | the same bug with a numeric literal, so the fix is not text-only |
| =kv=, a =WITHOUT ROWID= user table | stored as an *index* b-tree, which =sqlite.rs= cannot walk. The resulting =Err= used to abort the whole container survey, and =container_drop_warnings= swallowed it -- so this one table silenced *every* defect 3 warning for the file |

*The =cities= layer is the common source's two rows*, so the non-ASCII and
leading-zero cases come along for free.

*Why the two live in one file:* they were found together, they are both
"the declaration survived and the value did not", and both are things a
GeoPackage acquires *after* GDAL wrote it -- which is the class the fixture
set had no member of at all.

/Rebuilding it:/ =ogr2ogr -f GPKG sqlite_altered.gpkg gdal_hostile.gpkg cities=,
then the three =sqlite3= statements above. Note =VACUUM= fails on this file
("attempt to write a readonly database"); the 128 KB size is in line with the
other =.gpkg= fixtures and was left alone.

*** =gdal_hostile.gpkg=
=ogr2ogr= plus =sqlite3= for the container content. Carries:
| content                          | why |
|----------------------------------+-----|
| two layers (=cities=, =second=)  | multi-layer container |
| =side_notes= plain user table    | not a layer at all; geosetta destroys it |
| =gpkg_metadata= + =_reference=   | dataset lineage |
| =gpkg_extensions= (2 rows)       | the *real* R*Tree registrations |
| R*Tree tables + triggers         | derived-capability |
| =gpkg_ogr_contents=              | derived-capability |
| =flag BOOLEAN= declared column   | defect 2 -- the declaration is on disk and unread |

*Extended 2026-08-21 for the GeoPackage spoke* (M3), which needed layer-level
members the file did not yet carry -- =identifier= was just the table name and
=description= was empty, so a fixture built to be hostile was exercising
neither:
| content                                  | why |
|------------------------------------------+-----|
| =cities.identifier= =Bykerne — København og Zürich= | a *non-default* title, and non-ASCII besides -- the writer used to hardcode =identifier = table_name= |
| =cities.description=                      | non-empty; the writer used to hardcode =""= |
| =gpkg_data_columns= (2 rows)              | column alias/title/comment, and a =constraint_name= reference |
| =gpkg_data_column_constraints= (1 row)    | the =price_range= domain those rows point at |
| =second=, left at =ogr2ogr='s defaults    | the *negative* case: identifier = table name, empty description, so D3's "carry nothing" path is exercised by the same file |

The identifier/description pair came from =ogr2ogr -lco IDENTIFIER= /
=-lco DESCRIPTION=; the two Schema-extension tables were authored with
=sqlite3=, because no =ogr2ogr= invocation writes one from a source that has
none. *Both were then verified through the reference tool*, which is what makes
them real rather than inert bytes -- =ogrinfo= reports
=alternative name="city_name"=, =comment=Municipality name ...= and
=domain name=price_range=, and =ogrinfo -fielddomain price_range= prints the
range and its description. A fixture GDAL ignores would prove nothing.

/The non-ASCII bytes were checked raw after writing/ (=b'Bykerne \xe2\x80\x94
K\xc3\xb8benhavn og Z\xc3\xbcrich'=), per the heredoc trap recorded above --
the additions were made with =python3= + =sqlite3= and explicit encoding, not
through a shell heredoc.

*A fake vendor row in =gpkg_extensions= was tried and removed.* With
=scope='read-write'=, GDAL refuses the layer entirely
(="relies on the 'example_vendor_ext' extension ... ERROR 1"=), which would make
the fixture unreadable by the reference tool. The two genuine R*Tree
registrations exercise =gpkg_extensions= preservation without that. *Do not
re-add a fake extension row.*

Read it with =--layer cities=: it is multi-layer, so a bare stdout conversion
correctly errors asking for a layer or a directory.

*** =gdal_hostile.shp= (+ =.shx=, =.dbf=, =.prj=, =.cpg=)
=ogr2ogr= Esri Shapefile with =-lco ENCODING=UTF-8=.
- =name/zip/note: String (80.0)= -- the *declared width*, which geosetta used
  to re-derive down to the current data. The single most workflow-breaking loss
  in the inventory, and *fixed 2026-08-20*: this fixture is now the one the
  =declared_shapefile_widths_survive_a_flatgeobuf_transit= test in
  =convert.rs= runs against, chosen because its values are 6 and 10 bytes long
  so the 80 cannot have come from the rows.
- =price: Real (24.15)= -- declared precision, which geosetta used to rewrite
  to =Real (8.6)= from a hardcoded =DECIMALS = 6=. Also fixed; a declared
  =scale= now replaces that constant.
- =flag: Integer(Boolean) (1.0)= -- Shapefile's boolean *subtype*.
- =.cpg= = =UTF-8= -- the declared codepage. Geosetta writes no =.cpg=; so does
  =ogr2ogr=, which is why the inventory ranks this below the width loss.
- =.prj= -- EPSG:4326, so the CRS path is exercised too.

*** =hand_hostile.kml=
Authored: =ogr2ogr='s KML writer emits none of the presentation tree, so a
hostile KML has to be written by hand. Verified that geosetta reads it and that
each element below is in fact dropped.
| carries                          | why |
|----------------------------------+-----|
| =<Style>= + =<styleUrl>=         | KML's whole point for many users |
| document =<name>= / =<description>= | the collection's own identity |
| =<Folder>= nesting               | flattened deliberately (=kml/reader.rs:49=) |
| =<visibility>=, =<TimeStamp>=    | per-Placemark presentation/time |
| =<altitudeMode>=                 | already an OPEN CANDIDATE in =lossy-conversion-warnings.org= |
| =<ExtendedData>= with =007=/=1.50= | survives, but coerced to strings |
| a =<Model>= Placemark            | an unmodelled geometry -- becomes =geometry: null= *silently* |
| a =<GroundOverlay>=              | *vanishes entirely* -- a georeferenced image, not decoration |

The =GroundOverlay= references =files/overlay.png=, which is why the KMZ below
carries that file: together they pin the dangling-reference failure.

*** =hand_hostile.kmz=
=hand_hostile.kml= as =doc.kml=, plus =files/overlay.png= (a real 1×1 PNG, not a
text stub, so it is a plausible referenced asset) and =files/notes.txt=.
Geosetta writes =doc.kml= *alone*, so both sidecars are dropped and the
surviving KML keeps a reference to an image that is no longer in the archive.

This is the fixture for the container obligation that
=same-format-fidelity.org= M3c added after the inventory found that KMZ is a
container on the same terms as GeoPackage.

** REBUILDING
The GDAL-produced four come from the § THE COMMON SOURCE table via =ogr2ogr=
(Shapefile and GeoPackage direct; FlatGeobuf and GeoParquet *from the
GeoPackage*, which is what makes GDAL propagate metadata into them). The
authored five are written with explicit UTF-8 encoding -- *not* through a shell
heredoc, per § THE COMMON SOURCE.

If you rebuild any of them, re-check two things before committing: that the
non-ASCII bytes are still real UTF-8, and that geosetta still *reads* every
fixture without error.
